stem: A child with diabetic ketoacidosis has marked dehydration and severe circulatory impairment on arrival to the emergency department; what supportive measure is specifically indicated?

options.text: Discharge with sick-day advice once ketones are checked
Avoid all monitoring until venous blood gas results are back
Prioritise coeliac serology before cardiorespiratory support

explanation: Administer supplemental oxygen. Supplemental oxygen is specifically indicated when a child with diabetic ketoacidosis has severe circulatory impairment or shock, as part of immediate supportive care.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because supplemental oxygen is specifically indicated when severe circulatory impairment or shock is present in diabetic ketoacidosis.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a child with diabetic ketoacidosis and circulatory compromise should not have unrestricted oral intake immediately.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because this child is acutely unwell and needs emergency management, not discharge.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because monitoring and ABC assessment should proceed immediately rather than waiting for blood gas results.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because coeliac serology is not a priority over urgent cardiorespiratory support in circulatory compromise.
